title: StreamIterator: context-aware prefetch, per-message deadlines, and graceful Close semantics in Go SDK
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Current Go SDK streaming examples expose the raw transport recv/stream loop to consumers. This makes it easy to accidentally leak goroutines or mishandle per-request deadlines: callers either pass a single long-lived context or manage per-message deadlines awkwardly. We also observe poor tail latency when a single network hiccup stalls the foreground Read; conservative callers disable prefetch entirely and lose p50 throughput improvements.

Proposal: Implement a high-level StreamIterator abstraction that: (1) exposes Next(ctx) and Close(ctx) semantics familiar to Go developers, (2) performs an adaptive prefetch in a background goroutine to smooth transient network jitter while honoring per-message deadlines supplied via the call context, and (3) provides explicit Close/Abort policies so consumers can choose to drain or cancel in-flight prefetch. The iterator will publish observability metrics and be feature-flagged for gradual rollout.

Key behaviors: Next(ctx) blocks until one of: a prefetched item is available and still within its per-message deadline, the provided ctx is canceled/expired, or the underlying stream reports terminal error. Prefetch uses a bounded ring buffer; items that age past their per-message deadline are evicted and counted as dropped_prefetch. Close(ctx) negotiates shutdown: default policy attempts graceful drain for a short window (configurable), then cancels background fetch. API ergonomics modeled after bufio.Scanner but with context semantics: callers pass per-call ctx to express timeouts/cancellations.

Constraints and trade-offs: Prefetch reduces observed p50 while introducing complexity around per-item deadlines and memory buffering. We avoid unbounded buffering and keep internal concurrency low (1 prefetch goroutine per StreamIterator by default). We must be careful about races between Close and Next, and about not blocking Close() indefinitely.
acceptance_criteria: Public API: StreamIterator type with NewStreamIterator(stream, opts), Next(ctx) (returns (Message, error)), and Close(ctx) documented and vetted
Per-call ctx respected: when Next(ctx) returns due to ctx.Done(), no goroutine or buffer leak remains
Adaptive prefetch: default prefetch window improves p50 by >=20% for our synthetic jitter workload with <=1KB messages
Eviction semantics: prefetched messages older than their per-message deadline are evicted and emitted via metric dropped_prefetch
Comprehensive unit and integration tests covering race windows, Close() during inflight prefetch, and per-message timeout eviction
Benchmarks added to repo/bench/ showing baseline vs prefetch P50/P95 numbers and memory impact
Documentation and migration guide for callers currently using raw Recv loops
Feature flag exists and rollout plan documented in the ticket
decisions: Expose per-call ctx only (avoid embedding timeouts into iterator constructor) to keep API ergonomic and explicit
Single background prefetch goroutine per iterator by default to simplify locking and avoid thread explosion
Bound prefetch buffer with adaptive target (min=1, default=4, max=16) based on observed recv latency and client-specified hints
Evict prefetched items whose per-message deadline has elapsed rather than returning stale messages to callers
Metrics to emit: prefetch_inflight, prefetch_evictions, prefetch_latency_p50/p90, iterator_next_latency_p50/p95, iterator_close_duration
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Initial ticket created after spike showing callers mishandling cancellation and leaking goroutines in common usage patterns.

2025-02-15: Spike implemented prototype: background fetch + ring buffer + eviction. Ran microbenchmarks against synthetic jitter generator. Observed ~24% p50 improvement for small payloads, p95 similar to baseline when eviction enabled.

2025-02-20: Design review with Priya Nair and Alex Wu. Priya requested clearer semantics for Close(ctx) (drain vs abort) and an explicit Abort() helper. Alex asked for stronger guarding against double-Close and idempotency guarantees.
2025-02-25: Iteration 1 PR opened implementing StreamIterator with opts for BufferSize and ClosePolicy (DrainTimeout). Included unit tests for eviction behavior.
2025-03-03: Added integration tests against the real hosted API using test harness. Fixed race condition where Next() could block indefinitely if Close() raced with a prefetch write to the channel.
2025-03-05: PR updated with requested API docs and bench results. Marked as In Review and requested Diego for final signoff on locking semantics.
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/1452 - fix: prevent Next() indefinite block on Close race
tests_and_benchmarks: unit: TestStreamIterator_Next_ContextCancel - verifies no goroutine leaks when Next(ctx) canceled
unit: TestStreamIterator_PrefetchEviction - verifies stale messages are not returned
integration: TestStreamIterator_AgainstHosted - exercise real network jitter using chaos worker
bench: BenchmarkIterator_NoPrefetch vs BenchmarkIterator_Prefetch - p50 improvement ~24% for 256B messages, memory overhead < 8KB per iterator
race: run with -race in CI for three hours on linux-race runners to catch subtle handoff races
migration_notes: For callers using raw Recv loops: Replace loop with it := NewStreamIterator(stream, nil); for { msg, err := it.Next(ctx); if err != nil { break } /* handle msg */ } it.Close(context.Background())
If callers relied on previously reading a stale prefetched value, audit for assumptions: StreamIterator will not return messages older than the deadline on the Next(ctx) call
Default Close policy drains for 250ms before aborting; callers needing immediate cancel should call Abort() (implemented as Close(ctx) with zero timeout)
followups: ENG-906100 - expose iterator metrics to console per-route
ENG-908300 - add TypeScript SDK parity for StreamIterator ergonomics
comments: Priya Nair (2025-02-20): Can we make Close() idempotent and ensure Abort() is a cheap signal? Also please add an example in examples/stream_iterator/main.go.
Alex Wu (2025-02-21): Suggest wrapping the prefetched item with a monotonic arrival timestamp to simplify eviction checks; avoid comparing wall-clock times directly.

Diego Martínez (2025-02-28): Found race in CI: prefetch goroutine writing to buffer while Close clears it. PR 1452 addresses this by using a single mutex around buffer state + closed flag. LGTM after tests pass.
Priya Nair (2025-03-04): Reviewed docs and migration guide. Request one more example showing per-call timeouts (ctx with 150ms deadline).
Diego Martínez (2025-03-05): Approving for merge on green. Assigning to release branch manager for canary rollout planning.
